rows.obligation: Field/integer conversion: every committed plane is a canonical Goldilocks residue and its integer meaning is the canonical lift of the table value it is looked up against
rows.source: hashline/src/field.rs:27-34 (`Fp::new`, `Fp::from_i64`), :199-203 (`Fp2::from_bytes` reduces once, does not reject); hashline/src/public_block_wire.rs:213-216 and :396-400 (wire `fp` rejects words >= P); attention.rs:1271-1285 (`fill` writes `Fp::from_i64`); attention.rs:2729-2778 (LogUp identity, table rows via `Tbl::row` 890-898 and `Fp2::from_i64`)
rows.parameter_assumption: Goldilocks p = 2^64-2^32+1; every table value |v| < 2^16 so the map v -> Fp::from_i64(v) is injective on each table
rows.evidence: A committed field element passes a lookup only if it equals Fp::from_i64(v) for some table row v (LogUp multiset argument, R12-R14). Integer semantics therefore hold for every looked-up plane; planes that are not looked up (zsel, E, m, Sum, D, Dsq, a1, a2) get their integer meaning from other relations (R09, R16-R19). The B4/B5 byte decoder rejects non-canonical words before any verifier runs (public_block_wire.rs:396-400).
rows.remaining_gap: The legacy `Fp2::from_bytes`/`AttnProof::to_bytes` flat encodings have no decoder and would silently alias words in [P, 2^64) to canonical values; they are not on the B4/B5 path. Typed (in-process) B3 verification accepts whatever `Fp` the caller constructs; no typed-API canonicality check exists (H1 report states this).

rows.evidence: D is NOT range-checked directly. Even branch (a1+a2 even): D = (a1+a2)/2 <= 2^32-1, D^2 <= (2^32-1)^2 = p - 2^32 < p, a1 + D^2 < p, so SSe = a1 + D^2 and a2 = 2D - a1 hold over the integers and force D = isqrt(SSe): EXACT. Odd branch: D = k + (p-1)/2 with k^2 - k + a1 = SSe + (p-1)/4 satisfies the SS sumcheck, both isqrt pins, the Square check and the a1/a2 limb ranges for EVERY int16 row (k = 2^31 whenever SS < 2^30; python scan: 100% of random rows admit a limb-range pair). It also satisfies NormDiv with y = 0 on every element, with rho = 2Cn x g + (2k-1)2^(tn-1) ~ 2^(31+tn). The fixed profile excludes it ONLY because rho ~ 2^42 exceeds the 2^32 two-limb range (margin 2^10). At tn = 0 the alias is excluded instead by the (p-1)/2 term of D*2^0 in NormDiv.
rows.remaining_gap: SOUNDNESS GAP FOR OTHER PROFILES: any profile with n_limbs >= 3 (wrho > 32, e.g. an Int24 residual class at d = 4096: D <= 2^29, tn = 7 -> dvp = 2^37) and tn >= 1 accepts an all-zero norm output row (concrete counterexample reproduced in results/zk60_fable_fa5_isqrt_alias.txt). Fix candidates: a direct range fact on D (U16 lookup at this profile; U16+U8 limbs generally) or a parity/small-range fact on a1+a2. Until then the fixed profile's exactness rests on the (tn, n_limbs) coincidence derived here, which no source comment or test records.
rows.derivation: p = 1 mod 4; inv(2) = (p+1)/2, inv(4) = (3p+1)/4. For a1+a2 = 2k-1 odd: D = k + (p-1)/2, D^2 = k^2 - k + inv(4) mod p, so a1 + D^2 = SSe forces a1 + k^2 - k = SSe + (p-1)/4 (unique integer in range since LHS < 2^64+2^32 < SSe + (p-1)/4 + p). (p-1)/4 = 2^62 - 2^30, so k = 2^31 for SSe < 2^30 and a1 = 2^30 + SSe, a2 = 2^32 - 1 - a1, both < 2^32. NormDiv with y=0: rho = 2Cn x g + D*2^tn = 2Cn x g + (2k-1)*2^(tn-1) (mod p, exact integer for tn >= 1); sigma = (2k-1)*2^(tn-1) - 1 - 2Cn x g. Both ~ 2^(31+tn): 2^42 at tn = 11 > 2^32 (two limbs) but < 2^48 (three limbs).
rows.severity: HIGH for deployment profiles with n_limbs >= 3; NONE for the fixed profile (excluded by derivation); documentation/test debt for the fixed profile
